xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4762: File links: add Open in browser and Open in <Browser> to the right-click menu

plan.title: File links: add Open in browser and Open in <Browser> to the right-click menu
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: Right-clicking a file chip in a conversation offers editor, containing-folder and copy actions only. An HTML mockup, SVG, PDF or image cannot be opened in a web browser with one click; the operator copies the path into a browser by hand.
narratives.Proposal: Add a BROWSERS list (separate from EDITORS) to packages/contracts/src/editor.ts. PanOpenLive detects browsers once at layer build (Linux: command on PATH; macOS: /Applications/<App>.app via async fs.access; Windows: default only) and caches a Map<BrowserId, launcher>. New PanOpen methods getAvailableBrowsers() and openInBrowser({ path, browser }) spawn only detected launchers with a pathToFileURL file:// URL. New RPCs pan.getAvailableBrowsers and pan.shellOpenInBrowser are wired in ws-rpc.ts with no-loss-matrix rows. MarkdownFileLink adds 'Open in browser' plus one 'Open in <Browser>' item per detected browser to both right-click menus, after the editor items and before 'Open containing folder', only for html/htm/xhtml/svg/pdf/png/jpg/jpeg/gif/webp/avif/md/txt chips, using filePath. docs/MARKDOWN-EDITOR-PANE.md documents the new items. Full detail, snippets and line references are in .pan/drafts/PAN-4762.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Resolving the OS's real default browser for default-browser (xdg-settings get default-web-browser, macOS LaunchServices); default-browser uses xdg-open/open/explorer as the issue specifies
- Detecting named browsers on Windows (Windows offers only Open in browser)
- Opening the browser on the viewer's machine when the dashboard is viewed remotely (Anywhere work)
- Opening workspace dev-server http:// URLs in a browser
- Adding browsers to EDITORS, PanOpenInPicker, EditorPane.tsx, keybindings.ts or the resolvePreferredEditor() fallback
- Persisting a last-browser preference or letting a browser become the markdown left-click target (browser items never call setMarkdownOpenTarget)
- Browser items for .mdx, .markdown, .json, .log or any extension outside the issue's 13-extension list
- Changing launchDetached or adding an error handler to it
- Raising any cap in scripts/file-size-allowlist.txt
- Committing packages/contracts/dist/ (it is gitignored)

autoDecisions.summary: default-browser hands the file:// URL to the platform opener exactly as the issue says (xdg-open on Linux, open on macOS, explorer on Windows).
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue names this mechanism explicitly. These openers choose the app by file type, so for non-HTML types (png, pdf, md, txt) the OS may open a non-browser app; that limitation is documented and resolving the real default browser is listed as a non-goal rather than built unasked.

autoDecisions.summary: BROWSERS entries use linuxCommands: string[] and macApp: string | null instead of EDITORS' single command field.
autoDecisions.rationale: Chromium ships as chromium or chromium-browser and macOS launches by app name with open -a, so a single command string cannot express the issue's own requirements.

autoDecisions.summary: Windows detects no named browsers; it offers only Open in browser.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue specifies Linux commands and macOS app paths only; 'where google-chrome' does not find Chrome on Windows.

autoDecisions.summary: default-browser's label is the lowercase word 'browser'.
autoDecisions.rationale: Menu text is uniformly `Open in ${label}` and toasts `Opened in ${label}`, which yields the issue's exact 'Open in browser' text with no special case.

autoDecisions.summary: Browser labels are Google Chrome, Chromium, Firefox, Brave, Microsoft Edge, Vivaldi; macOS app names add 'Brave Browser'.
autoDecisions.rationale: These are the product names the issue lists and the real /Applications bundle names.

autoDecisions.summary: The browser list is fetched only for browser-renderable chips; other chips keep the synchronous generic menu.
autoDecisions.rationale: Avoids an RPC round trip for menus that would show no browser items and keeps the existing synchronous menu test valid.

autoDecisions.summary: .mdx and .markdown chips get no browser items even though they use the markdown menu.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue's extension list includes md only.

autoDecisions.summary: openInBrowser rejects a non-absolute path before building the file:// URL.
autoDecisions.rationale: pathToFileURL silently resolves a relative path against the server's cwd, which would open the wrong file.

autoDecisions.summary: The new RPC methods keep the default admin scope and get OUT_OF_SCOPE no-loss-matrix rows.
autoDecisions.rationale: Matches shellOpenInEditor/getAvailableEditors; RPC_METHOD_SCOPES defaults every unlisted method to admin, and the matrix test fails without rows.

autoDecisions.summary: Failure toast text is `Failed to open in ${label}: <message>`.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue requires a failure toast without fixing its text; this mirrors the success toast and the existing 'Failed to open ...' pattern in the file.
grep -rn 'Open containing folder' docs configuration reference finds only that file, so the issue's fallback (conversation docs page) does not apply.

metadata.sizeJustification: Seven small vertical items across contracts, one server service, RPC wiring, one frontend component and one doc; well under the 25-file / 6-subsystem limits.

items.title: Add the BROWSERS list, BrowserIdSchema and OpenInBrowserInput to contracts

narrative.Action: Follow PRD WI-1. Append to packages/contracts/src/editor.ts, after OpenInEditorInput, the BROWSERS const (ids in order: default-browser, chrome, chromium, firefox, brave, edge, vivaldi; fields id, label, linuxCommands, macApp exactly as the PRD snippet), BrowserEntry, BrowserId, the BROWSER_IDS tuple, BrowserIdSchema = Schema.Literals(BROWSER_IDS), and OpenInBrowserInput = Schema.Struct({ path: Schema.String, browser: BrowserIdSchema }) with its type. Do NOT touch EDITORS or EditorIdSchema. index.ts already re-exports ./editor. Create packages/contracts/src/__tests__/browsers.test.ts with the four tests listed in WI-1.

narrative.Action: Follow PRD WI-2. In open.ts import access from node:fs/promises and BROWSERS/BrowserEntry/BrowserId from @overdeck/contracts; add BrowserLauncher, detectBrowserLauncher (default-browser: getFileManagerCommand() + isCommandAvailable; linux: first linuxCommands entry found by isCommandAvailable; darwin: await access('/Applications/<macApp>.app') -> { command: 'open', args: ['-a', macApp] }; other platforms: null) and resolveAvailableBrowsers returning Map<BrowserId, BrowserLauncher> in BROWSERS order. Add getAvailableBrowsers to PanOpenShape; in PanOpenLive compute cachedBrowsers after cachedEditors, log '[pan/open] Detected browsers: ...', return [...cachedBrowsers.keys()]. No sync fs or child_process calls. In open.test.ts add a mockAccess + vi.mock('node:fs/promises') and the Linux / chromium-browser / macOS / Windows detection tests, restoring process.platform in afterEach. Remember the node:util mock makes promisify(exec) and promisify(execFile) the same mockExecAsync.

items.title: Given Linux with firefox detected, when openInBrowser({ path: '/tmp/mock up/index.html', browser: 'firefox' }) runs, then spawn is called with 'firefox', ['file:///tmp/mock%20up/index.html'], { detached: true, stdio: 'ignore' }

Given an undetected browser ('vivaldi') or a relative path ('docs/a.html'), when openInBrowser runs, then the Effect exits with Failure carrying code BROWSER_LAUNCH_FAILED and spawn is never called
Add pan.getAvailableBrowsers and pan.shellOpenInBrowser RPCs with ws-rpc handlers and no-loss rows

narrative.Action: Follow PRD WI-4. In rpc.ts extend the ./editor import with BrowserIdSchema and OpenInBrowserInput; add WS_METHODS shellOpenInBrowser: 'pan.shellOpenInBrowser' and getAvailableBrowsers: 'pan.getAvailableBrowsers' after getAvailableEditors; add ShellOpenInBrowserRpc (payload OpenInBrowserInput, error PanRpcError) and GetAvailableBrowsersRpc (success Schema.Struct({ browsers: Schema.Array(BrowserIdSchema) })) after GetAvailableEditorsRpc; add both to the PanRpcGroup list after GetAvailableEditorsRpc. In ws-rpc.ts add the two handlers after the getAvailableEditors handler (shellOpenInBrowser -> panOpen.openInBrowser(input); getAvailableBrowsers -> panOpen.getAvailableBrowsers().pipe(Effect.map((browsers) => ({ browsers })))). Add nothing else to ws-rpc.ts (1136 lines, cap 1221). Add the two OUT_OF_SCOPE rows to tests/unit/lib/overdeck/no-loss-matrix.ts after the pan.getAvailableEditors row. route-scopes.ts needs no change (default admin scope).
